rules.description: it implements the closed load gates, smallest-owner confinement, reference closure, Schema Object dialect, and selector semantics of §§3–6.
it accepts only §7's envelope, applies §8's effective-parameter, collision, conversion, collection, location, empty, and form rules, and refuses every unknown or unroutable input before dispatch.

it preserves media alternatives and applies §9's matching, request election, carriage, content-coding, response lookup, classification, and unary-boundary rules without sniffing or undeclared fallback.
it resolves complete target URLs under §10 and security alternatives, credentials, prerequisites, and channel collisions under §11.
§3.2's source, addressability, synthesis-status, and invocation-outcome axes remain independent, including when every addressable target is invalid or excluded.
§11 rejects an invalid API-key header name as an excluded security alternative and rejects an unsafe runtime header value before dispatch.
an invalid failure-only Response projection remains coverage loss without removing its operation, as §9.4 requires.
§9.4 performs no content decoding or output for HEAD, non-101 informational, `204`, `205`, and `304` responses and reports forbidden actual content as a loud response-phase protocol error.
a declared body projection cannot cause content decoding or output for an actual no-content response.
§8.2 excludes a non-token optional ordinary-header projection without excluding the operation, allowing an invocation that omits it to dispatch.
§8.2 treats the would-be caller key of that excluded optional header as unknown input and refuses it before dispatch.
§8.2 propagates a non-token required ordinary header to an excluded target that remains addressable and refuses before dispatch.
§8.2 prevents caller control of every listed connection, framing, routing, and selected-body-media field by excluding the addressable target before dispatch.
§9.4 treats `101 Switching Protocols` as an immediate loud response-phase protocol error rather than waiting for a later HTTP final response.
§9.4 admits a `default`-only Responses Object and uses that Response Object for an otherwise unmatched successful status.

§§8.2 and 11 refuse any supplied ordinary-header or header-credential value that is not an RFC 9110 `field-value`, including leading or trailing SP or HTAB, and additionally require a raw `Cookie` field value to be an RFC 6265 `cookie-string`.

§9.4 confines invalid Response keys, values, and fixed members to their smallest projections without changing admitted-key precedence or removing an otherwise usable target; valid body and header siblings still govern, matched-but-excluded media fails loudly only when selected on success, and failure decoding remains best-effort.

§9.3 groups surviving response Header declarations by ASCII-case-insensitive field identity, applies every `Content-Encoding` constraint conjunctively, and never excludes an OAS 2.0 response merely because optional case-equivalent declarations conflict.
§11 confines statically unavoidable credential collisions to the smallest security alternative and preserves every non-colliding OR alternative.
§11 checks actual serialized destinations and treats optional or runtime-derived parameter collisions as invocation-conditional rather than static exclusions.
§§8.2 and 11 reserve each processor-owned header destination, including `Proxy-Authorization`, at the target or security-alternative boundary.
§11 percent-encodes both an API-key query name and value with uppercase UTF-8 triplets.
§11 preserves the unordered multiset of ordinary-parameter and credential query contributions and each contribution's fixed bytes.
§10 rejects an empty artifact host and refuses any completed or configured HTTP URL without a nonempty host or with userinfo before dispatch.
§8.3 emits generated multipart `name` parameters with the pinned UTF-8 quoted-string escaping and excludes a name outside that admitted byte grammar.
§9.4 strips binding-selected header credentials and Cookie contributions on a followed cross-origin redirect and never appends a binding-selected query credential to any redirect Location.
§9.3 refuses a supplied request `Content-Encoding` field on a body-free invocation and excludes a required field only when no surviving request lane can emit a representation.
§11 constructs OAuth2 Bearer authorization from one valid RFC 6750 `b64token` and refuses every empty, non-Bearer-typed, or grammatically invalid token before dispatch.
§9.3 validates no-content response `Content-Encoding` syntax and exact raw-string domains without requiring or invoking a decoder.

§9.2 requires UTF-8 encoding and decoding, treats additional charset directions as independent capabilities, refuses an unavailable or failed request encoder before dispatch, and reports an unavailable or failed response decoder loudly.
§9.3 derives response `Content-Encoding` raw-string domains by filtering a string Header's enum to string members and applies every case-folded group's domains conjunctively at response time.
§9.2 refuses before dispatch a caller-supplied JSON value containing an unpaired surrogate code unit, without replacement, passthrough, or request-byte emission.
§7 computes caller-key uniqueness only after invalid and excluded parameter projections are removed, so a removed projection creates no key and does not activate qualified mode.

§8.2 emits the deterministic equal-preference `Accept` union for admitted response media, while an effective OAS 2.0 Header Parameter whose name compares ASCII case-insensitively to `Accept` suppresses generation and retains ordinary caller ownership.
§10 confines an out-of-enum authored `schemes` member to that invalid alternative, preserves valid siblings, and retains complete-URL recovery when no dispatchable artifact alternative survives.

§8.2 excludes a response media range carrying a case-insensitive `q` parameter only when the binding generates `Accept`, preserves every valid sibling range, and keeps that range admitted when an effective caller-owned Header Parameter whose name compares ASCII case-insensitively to `Accept` suppresses generation.

it preserves §12.2's binding/transform boundary, emits no artifact-derived inbound dependency, accounts every lossy or non-equivalent Schema Object translation as coverage loss, and reports complete operation coverage under Core OBI-B-02.
it uses §3.2's locally defined status vocabulary for targets and subordinate projections without depending on any project interface contract.
§9.4's declared body projection for a no-content response is subordinate `excluded` coverage while the operation remains represented.
§9.3 confines a non-token response Header Object key to subordinate `excluded` coverage without removing the response alternative or operation.
§9.4 represents an otherwise usable operation whose Responses Object is `default`-only and projects that fallback Response Object normally.
§9.4 retains an operation and every valid response sibling while accounting each invalid or excluded response projection at its smallest owner.
§11 removes only statically unavoidable credential-collision alternatives, preserves non-colliding OR alternatives, and never treats an optional parameter collision as a static exclusion.
§8.3 accounts an unrepresentable multipart name at its media-alternative owner while preserving unrelated operations.
§9.3 accounts a required bodyless request `Content-Encoding` parameter at its target owner while preserving unrelated operations.
§7 derives the operation input from the post-confinement effective parameter set, leaving a surviving same-named cross-location parameter unqualified when its only collision was removed.

§10 accounts an out-of-enum authored `schemes` member as invalid at that alternative while retaining valid siblings or a represented target with its actual `configuration.server` recovery requirement.

§8.2 accounts a response media range carrying a case-insensitive `q` parameter as excluded only when generated `Accept` would carry it, while preserving a valid sibling or, under effective caller ownership of `Accept`, that same range and its target.

§10 excludes only an unusable declaration-derived Server alternative with query, fragment, empty HTTP host, or userinfo, permits a sibling or complete configured URL to recover, and refuses a nonconforming consumer choice before dispatch.

§10 accounts a Server Variable Object with an absent or wrong-typed required `default` as `invalid` at its Server alternative while retaining a target recoverable through `configuration.server`.
§10 excludes an empty variable `enum` or out-of-enum declaration default at its Server alternative while retaining siblings and complete-URL recovery.
§10 permits an exact consumer substitution for an otherwise undeclared Server URL expression and reports a missing substitution as context-required on `configuration.server`.
§10 refuses a consumer substitution outside a declared nonempty variable `enum` without changing synthesis coverage or weakening the selected Server Object.

§7 computes caller-key uniqueness only after invalid and excluded parameter projections are removed, so a removed projection creates no key and does not activate qualified mode.

§9.1 emits the deterministic equal-preference `Accept` union of every admitted response-content media range across successful and unsuccessful response alternatives and omits it only when that set is empty.
§9.3 invents neither `filename` nor `filename*`, preserves an admissible artifact-fixed literal `filename`, and excludes a fixed `filename*` at the multipart alternative.
§9.1 excludes a response media range carrying a case-insensitive `q` parameter before `Accept` construction while preserving every valid sibling range.
§8.3 keeps form-cookie array and object declarations represented without shape-only exclusion, including their required forms and both `explode` choices.

§8.3 refuses only a supplied form-cookie value whose actual expansion represents multiple logical values, while a zero- or one-pair expansion remains available subject to the ordinary cookie-name and value checks.
§8.2 refuses a supplied nested array or object member whose runtime shape leaves the admitted style cell, without private stringification or JSON serialization.

§9.1 applies required-body exclusion to the effective post-method, post-confinement request-content set, while preserving a method-ignored body declaration and every surviving configurable alternative.
§9.1 advertises an admitted failure-only response media range in `Accept` without allowing that range to govern an actual successful response.
